**Yes, if you’re new to Chase and can meet its monthly cashback rules.** Comparing the free UK accounts as of **21 November 2026**, I’d pick Chase for everyday spending and first-year easy-access savings. Monzo pays the better standard savings rate once Chase’s introductory boost ends. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/legal/cashback-terms-and-conditions/))

**Cashback:** Chase pays **2%, capped at £20 a month**, on eligible card spending including groceries, restaurants, takeaways, public transport (including TfL), fuel and public EV charging. So £500 a month of eligible spending earns **£10**; £1,000 earns the full **£20**. After a joining grace period, you qualify for the *following* month by keeping **at least £1,000 in Chase savers every day** and making **at least 15 card payments or Direct Debits** that month. Direct Debits count towards the 15 but don’t earn cashback themselves. Monzo instead gives you retailer-specific offers to activate in the app: useful when one matches a purchase you already plan to make, but less predictable for the weekly shop. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/legal/cashback-terms-and-conditions/))

**Savings:** The better choice depends on how you save:

| What you’re saving | Better choice between the two |
|---|---|
| A lump sum you want available immediately | **Chase if you’re new:** open its boosted saver within 31 days of joining for **4.75% AER variable**, including a 12-month boost. Free Monzo Instant Access pays **2.80% AER variable**. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/saver-boosted/)) |
| A lump sum without the Chase boost | **Monzo:** its **2.80%** beats Chase’s standard **2.50%**. Monzo Select Access pays **3.45% AER variable** if you deposit at least £500 and make no more than two withdrawals per year. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/saver-boosted/)) |
| Money you put aside each payday | **Chase Regular Saver:** **6.50% AER fixed for 12 months** on deposits of up to **£300 a month**, with withdrawals allowed. That rate is for monthly contributions, not a whole lump sum on day one. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/product/regular-saver/)) |

If you already use Monzo, **I wouldn’t move everything**. I’d use Chase for eligible spending and the boosted saver, then review the savings rate after 12 months. At today’s rates, keeping the £1,000 cashback minimum in Chase’s *standard* saver rather than Monzo Instant Access costs only **£3 a year** in interest before tax. The more important question is whether you’ll naturally make those 15 payments each month. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/legal/cashback-terms-and-conditions/))
